claim: Huck Finn is drawn from life; Tom Sawyer also, but not from an individual, and the author met him first in the summer of 1876.
notes: SUPPORTED: the prefatory note states verbatim 'Huck Finn is drawn from life; Tom Sawyer also, but not from an individual'. NOT SUPPORTED: the text gives no year for when the author met him; the 1876 date appears nowhere.
supported_clauses: Huck Finn is drawn from life; Tom Sawyer also, but not from an individual
unsupported_clauses: the author met him first in the summer of 1876

claim: Tom Sawyer belongs to the composite order of architecture, and he attends a boarding school in St. Louis.
notes: SUPPORTED: the prefatory note says Tom Sawyer 'belongs to the composite order of architecture'. NOT SUPPORTED: the text never places Tom at a boarding school; school scenes are at home with Aunt Polly and in the schoolhouse garden, not St. Louis.
supported_clauses: belongs to the composite order of architecture
unsupported_clauses: he attends a boarding school in St. Louis

claim: Tom Sawyer is a combination of the characteristics of three boys the author knew, and he later travels by raft down the Mississippi.
notes: SUPPORTED: verbatim in the prefatory note. NOT SUPPORTED: Tom's river episode is by raft on the Missouri, and the text describes no Mississippi raft voyage for him.
supported_clauses: a combination of the characteristics of three boys whom I knew
unsupported_clauses: he later travels by raft down the Mississippi

claim: Mr. Bennet's experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character, and he was elected to the position of hereditary sheriff.
notes: SUPPORTED: the opening paragraph states this almost verbatim. NOT SUPPORTED: Mr. Bennet is a gentleman of small income who lives on his estate; the text never says he holds the hereditary shrievalty office.
supported_clauses: the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character
unsupported_clauses: he was elected to the position of hereditary sheriff

claim: Bingley had not been of age two years when he was tempted by an accidental recommendation to look at Netherfield House, and he had already purchased a carriage of his own.
notes: SUPPORTED: stated in the opening chapter. NOT SUPPORTED: Bingley arrives by his own carriage later, but the text never says he had purchased one before renting Netherfield.
supported_clauses: Bingley had not been of age two years when he was tempted, by an accidental recommendation
unsupported_clauses: he had already purchased a carriage of his own

claim: Holmes met Irene Adler during a lengthy visit to Warsaw some five years earlier, and he describes her as being of Parisian birth.
notes: SUPPORTED: verbatim opening of 'A Scandal in Bohemia'. NOT SUPPORTED: the story gives her as having 'been born in Paris' only via Holmes's remark about her letters, and the narrator never states a birthplace as a description; the sentence as framed attributes a narration the story does not contain.
supported_clauses: Some five years ago, during a lengthy visit to Warsaw, I made the acquaintance of the well-known adventuress, Irene Adler
unsupported_clauses: he describes her as being of Parisian birth

claim: The society admits any red-headed man who is sound in body and mind and above twenty-one, and their membership requires a fee paid in cash.
notes: SUPPORTED: verbatim from 'The Red-Headed League'. NOT SUPPORTED: Holmes declines to join and is never charged; no membership fee appears anywhere in the story.
supported_clauses: All red-headed men who are sound in body and mind and above the age of twenty-one years, are eligible
unsupported_clauses: their membership requires a fee paid in cash

claim: Holmes requires his clients to bind themselves to absolute secrecy for two years, after which the matter is of no importance.
notes: SUPPORTED: the narrator's summary in 'The Red-Headed League' states this. NOT SUPPORTED: no retainer or refund arrangement appears in the story.
supported_clauses: binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance
unsupported_clauses: after which he returns any money they paid him as a retainer

claim: Alice felt a little nervous about shrinking further, and the first thing she drinks is a bottle of diluted vinegar.
notes: SUPPORTED: she says 'for it might end, you know ... in my going out altogether, like a candle'. NOT SUPPORTED: the drink that makes her shrink is labelled 'DRINK ME' on a paper label and is not identified as vinegar; the word vinegar appears nowhere in the text. An earlier draft asserted the bottle was UNLABELLED, which the text contradicts - it explicitly carries a 'DRINK ME' label.
supported_clauses: she felt a little nervous about this
unsupported_clauses: the first thing she drinks is a bottle of diluted vinegar

claim: Alice eats a cake and shrinks, and afterwards she attends a tea party with the Mad Hatter in a village governed by a crooked queen.
notes: SUPPORTED: eating the cake is stated. NOT SUPPORTED: the Hatter's party is held under the Hatter's own roof, and the queen's village is a separate later episode; no single village is governed by her in the tea-party scene.
supported_clauses: She ate a little bit, and said anxiously to herself
unsupported_clauses: she attends a tea party with the Mad Hatter in a village governed by a crooked queen
